prompt.text: Evaluate z₁ + z₂ if z₁ = 3 + 4i and z₂ = 2 − i. Give your answer in the form a + bi.

hints: Add the two real parts together, and separately add the two imaginary parts.
The real parts are 3 and 2. The imaginary parts are 4 and −1.

solution.text: Add real parts and imaginary parts separately.

prompt.text: Evaluate z₁ − z₂ if z₁ = 13 − 14i and z₂ = 22 + i. Give your answer in the form a + bi.

hints: Subtract the real parts, and separately subtract the imaginary parts.
Be careful with the sign of the imaginary part of z₂: it is +1, so you subtract 1 from −14.

solution.text: Subtract real parts and imaginary parts separately.

prompt.text: Find the conjugate of z = (4 − 6i) − (1 − i). Give your answer in the form a + bi.

hints: First simplify z by subtracting real parts and imaginary parts separately.
Once z is in the form x + yi, the conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part only.

solution.text: Change the sign of the imaginary part.
Alternatively, conjugate each number first, since conjugation distributes over subtraction.

prompt.text: Evaluate z₁ · z₂ if z₁ = 3 + 4i and z₂ = 2 − i. Give your answer in the form a + bi.

hints: Expand the brackets: multiply each term of the first number by each term of the second.
You will get a term in i². Replace i² with −1.
3·2 + 3·(−i) + 4i·2 + 4i·(−i). Collect the real terms and the terms in i.

solution.text: Replace i² with −1 and collect terms.
Check against the formula (ac − bd) + (bc + ad)i with a = 3, b = 4, c = 2, d = −1.

prompt.text: Evaluate z₁ · z₂ if z₁ = 11i + 4 and z₂ = −3 − 2i. Give your answer in the form a + bi.

hints: Write z₁ in the usual order first: z₁ = 4 + 11i. Then expand the brackets term by term.
Four products: 4·(−3), 4·(−2i), 11i·(−3), 11i·(−2i). The last one contains i².
11i·(−2i) = −22i² = +22. Now collect the real terms and the terms in i, watching the signs.

solution.text: Replace i² with −1 and collect terms.
